subproblem.title: Orthonormal frames with the same span evaluate all n-covectors equally up to one global sign
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ, e : Fin n → Euclid P (= ℝ^P) be orthonormal families for the Euclidean inner product with span(range τ) = span(range e). Then one of the following holds: (1) α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = α(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) for every n-covector α; or (2) α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = −α(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) for every n-covector α. Here an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, that is, a continuous alternating n-linear map α : (Euclid P)^n → ℝ, and α(v) denotes its value on v : Fin n → Euclid P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ e : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ e → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α τ = α e) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α τ = -α e)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (two unit orientations of one n-plane differ by a sign), isolated as a statement about two orthonormal frames of the same subspace. Compare Simon Ch. 6, proof of the Rectifiability Theorem 8.1, where an approximate tangent plane is oriented by ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ for any orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τₙ of it (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2223–2226), and (27) of §5, where a face is oriented by e₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ eₙ (book/chapter-06.txt line 1851).

Notation. Let W := span(range e) ⊆ Euclid P. W carries the inner product restricted from Euclid P (Submodule.coe_inner), so inner products and norms of elements of W are computed in Euclid P. For an n-covector α and v : Fin n → Euclid P, α(v) is the value of α on v.

1. A basis of W from e. Since e is orthonormal, it is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). Let b := Module.Basis.span of this linear independence. This is a basis of W indexed by Fin n with b j = ⟨e j, subset_span (mem_range_self j)⟩ (Module.Basis.span_apply), so (b j : Euclid P) = e j (Module.Basis.coe_span_apply). Consequently finrank W = card(Fin n) = n (finrank_span_eq_card and Fintype.card_fin).

2. τ as a family in W. For each j, τ j ∈ span(range τ) = W by hypothesis (Submodule.subset_span). Let τ_W : Fin n → W be τ_W j := ⟨τ j, _⟩, so (τ_W j : Euclid P) = τ j.

3. Reduction to one determinant. Fix an n-covector α. Let α_W be the alternating n-linear map W^n → ℝ obtained by composing the underlying alternating map of α with the inclusion W.subtype: α_W := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap W.subtype. Thus α_W(w) = α(j ↦ (w j : Euclid P)) for every w : Fin n → W.
 Since b is a basis of W indexed by the same type Fin n, AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det gives α_W = α_W(b) • b.det, where b.det is the determinant alternating map of b. Evaluating both sides at τ_W:
 α_W(τ_W) = α_W(b) · b.det(τ_W).
 Here α_W(τ_W) = α(τ), because (τ_W j : Euclid P) = τ j, and α_W(b) = α(e), because (b j : Euclid P) = e j. So
 α(τ) = α(e) · c, where c := b.det(τ_W) ∈ ℝ.
 The number c depends only on b and τ_W, not on α.

4. c = ±1.
 (i) b is orthonormal in W. By step 1, b is the family j ↦ ⟨e j, _⟩ of span(range e), and this family is orthonormal because e is (orthonormal_span). So oe := b.toOrthonormalBasis is an orthonormal basis of W, and oe.toBasis = b (Module.Basis.toBasis_toOrthonormalBasis).
 (ii) τ_W is an orthonormal basis of W. τ_W is orthonormal in W because τ is orthonormal in Euclid P and inner products in W are those of Euclid P (Orthonormal.codRestrict). Hence τ_W is linearly independent. It has card(Fin n) = n = finrank W members (step 1), so span(range τ_W) = W (LinearIndependent.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank'). Thus oτ := OrthonormalBasis.mk is an orthonormal basis of W with ⇑oτ = τ_W (OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk).
 (iii) The change-of-basis determinant between two orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is ±1: its matrix is orthogonal, so its determinant squares to 1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real: oe.toBasis.det oτ = 1 ∨ oe.toBasis.det oτ = −1). By (i) and (ii), oe.toBasis.det oτ = b.det τ_W = c. Hence c = 1 or c = −1.

5. Conclusion. If c = 1, step 3 gives α(τ) = α(e) · 1 = α(e) for every n-covector α. If c = −1, step 3 gives α(τ) = α(e) · (−1) = −α(e) for every n-covector α. Since c does not depend on α, this is the required dichotomy.

6. The case n = 0 is included. Then W = {0}, b and τ_W are the empty family, and b.det(τ_W) = 1 (the determinant of the empty matrix), so the first alternative holds. The argument above covers this case without change. ∎

Formalization note: a direct Lean proof of this exact type following steps 1–5 (about 45 lines) compiled in the comparator's replayed Ch07 scope with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. In the evaluation of eq_smul_basis_det at τ_W, the hypothesis simplifies to α.toAlternatingMap (fun i => W.subtype (τW i)) = α.toAlternatingMap (fun i => W.subtype (b i)) * b.det τW; rewrite (fun i => W.subtype (τW i)) = τ by rfl and (fun i => W.subtype (b i)) = e by funext with step 1.
proof_key_steps: W := span(range e) has the basis b = Module.Basis.span (e is linearly independent) with b_j = e_j, and finrank W = n. Each τ_j lies in span(range τ) = W, giving τ_W : Fin n → W.
For each n-covector α, restrict it to W and apply AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis b. This gives α(τ) = α(e) · c with c := b.det(τ_W), which does not depend on α.
b and τ_W are orthonormal bases of W (τ_W spans because it has n = finrank W independent members). So c = oe.toBasis.det oτ ∈ {1, −1} by det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real.
c = 1 gives α(τ) = α(e) for all α, and c = −1 gives α(τ) = −α(e) for all α. The case n = 0 is included.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type require both orthonormality hypotheses and equal spans, with the disjunction correctly outside the universal covector quantifier. Restriction to the common span yields α(τ) = α(e)·c with c independent of α. Both frames give orthonormal bases there, so the cited determinant theorem gives c = ±1. The proof therefore establishes one global sign, includes n = 0, and has no circular reliance or missing construction.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes of a set lying in an affine plane x + V are contained in V
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, A ⊆ Euclid P (= ℝ^P), x ∈ Euclid P, and let Q and V be linear subspaces of Euclid P. Assume a − x ∈ V for every a ∈ A. Assume also that Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x in the sense of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4, as formalized in SimonGMT Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean). This means: (a) finrank Q = n, and (b) for every compactly supported continuous f : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺ (along the filter 𝓝[>] 0). Here η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) is blowUpMap x r, Hⁿ = μHE[n], each integral is taken against the restriction of Hⁿ to the indicated set, and no measurability of A is assumed. Then Q ⊆ V, i.e. Q ≤ V as submodules.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ a ∈ A, a - x ∈ V) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → Q ≤ V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof (blow-ups lie in the plane; the bump-function argument), stated for an arbitrary linear subspace V in place of the coordinate plane. Compare Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and the test-function argument of Remark 1.5(3) (book/chapter-03.txt lines 77–93).

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For r ∈ ℝ let S_r := blowUpMap x r '' A = {r⁻¹ • (a − x) : a ∈ A}. Let μ := Hⁿ.restrict Q, the restriction of Hⁿ to the set Q. Write (a) and (b) for the two components of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q.

1. Blow-ups lie in V. Let r ∈ ℝ and a ∈ A. By hypothesis a − x ∈ V, and V is closed under scalar multiplication, so blowUpMap x r a = r⁻¹ • (a − x) ∈ V (Submodule.smul_mem). Hence S_r ⊆ V for every r ∈ ℝ.

2. Set-up of a contradiction. Let q ∈ Q, and suppose q ∉ V. The subspace V of the finite-dimensional normed space Euclid P is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and it is nonempty since 0 ∈ V. Hence d := infDist(q, V) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).

3. A bump function. Define g : Euclid P → ℝ by g(y) := max(0, d/2 − dist(y, q)).
 (i) g is continuous, as the max of the constant 0 and the continuous function y ↦ d/2 − dist(y, q).
 (ii) g(y) ≥ 0 for every y.
 (iii) support g = ball(q, d/2): max(0, t) ≠ 0 iff t > 0, and d/2 − dist(y, q) > 0 iff dist(y, q) < d/2.
 (iv) g has compact support: if y ∉ closedBall(q, d/2), then dist(y, q) > d/2, so d/2 − dist(y, q) < 0 and g(y) = 0. Closed balls of Euclid P are compact (HasCompactSupport.intro with isCompact_closedBall).
 Therefore g underlies an element f of C_c(Euclid P, ℝ), namely the CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, (i)⟩, (iv)⟩, and f(y) = g(y) for all y.

4. g vanishes on V. Let v ∈ V. Then d = infDist(q, V) ≤ dist(q, v) = dist(v, q) (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). So d/2 − dist(v, q) ≤ −d/2 < 0, and g(v) = max(0, d/2 − dist(v, q)) = 0.

5. The blow-up integrals vanish. Fix r ∈ ℝ. Every y ∈ S_r lies in V by step 1, so f(y) = g(y) = 0 by step 4. Hence ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). This lemma needs no measurability of S_r. Indeed f vanishes at every point of S_r, so the open (hence Borel) set O := {f ≠ 0} satisfies (Hⁿ.restrict S_r)(O) = Hⁿ(O ∩ S_r) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply for the measurable set O). Thus f = 0 holds (Hⁿ.restrict S_r)-almost everywhere, and the integral is 0.

6. The plane integral is zero. Apply (b) to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0. By step 5 this function is identically 0, so it also tends to 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_const_nhds). The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff, so limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.

7. The plane measure charges every ball around q. By (a), finrank Q = n. Hence the support of μ = Hⁿ.restrict Q is exactly Q (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, SimonGMT Ch. 3). Since q ∈ Q, q lies in the support of μ, so every neighbourhood of q has positive μ-measure (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall). Because d/2 > 0, ball(q, d/2) is a neighbourhood of q (ball_mem_nhds), so μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0.

8. Integrability. By (a), μ is a regular measure (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. A continuous function with compact support is integrable for such a measure (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), so g is μ-integrable.

9. Positivity and contradiction. Since g ≥ 0 and g is μ-integrable, integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives: 0 < ∫ g dμ iff 0 < μ(support g).
